newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-DODGERS' HOLLANDSWORTH NAMED NL ROOKIE OF THE YEAR.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-DODGERS' HOLLANDSWORTH NAMED NL ROOKIE OF THE YEAR.

text.p: Los Angeles outfielder Todd
Hollandsworth on Wednesday became the fifth consecutive Dodger
to win the National League Rookie of the Year Award.
Hollandsworth received 15 first-place votes, nine seconds
and three thirds for 105 total points in balloting by a
28-member panel of the Baseball Writers' Association of
America.
Florida Marlins shortstop Edgar Renteria finished second
in the balloting with 10 first-place votes and 84 points,
while Pittsburgh Pirates catcher Jason Kendall was a distant
third with 30 points and just one first-place vote.
Montreal Expos outfielder F.P. Santangelo and New York
Mets shortstop Rey Ordonez each received one first-place vote.
Hollandsworth enjoyed a strong second half of the season
and finished with a .291 batting average, 12 homers, 21 stolen
bases, 64 runs and 59 Runs Batted In over 149 games.
He follows pitcher Hideo Nomo, outfielder Raul Mondesi,
catcher Mike Piazza and first baseman Eric Karros, breaking
the record for consecutive victories by one club for the
prestigious first-year honour.
The Dodgers organisation has produced a record 16 Rookies
of the Year, dating back to Brooklyn Dogers great Jackie
Robinson, who won the first award, which how bears his name,
Shortstop Derek Jeter, who helped the New York Yankees win
their first World Series in 18 years, was named American
League Rookie of the Year Monday by a unanimous vote.
Renteria was a .309 hitter with five homers, 31 RBI, 68
runs and 16 stolen bases in 106 contests. Kendall was named to
the NL All-Star team and hit .300 with three homers, 42 RBI
and 54 runs scored in 130 games.
Voting breakdown for the 1996 NL Rookie of the Year Award
in balloting by a 28-member panel of the Baseball Writers
Association of America (five points for first place, three for
second, one for third):
1 2 3 Total points
1. Todd Hollandsworth, Los 15 9 3 105
2. Edgar Renteria, Fla 10 10 4 84
3. Jason Kendall, Pit 1 5 10 30
4. F.P. Santangelo, Mon 1 2 4 15
5. Rey Ordonez, NYM 1 - 2 7
6. Jermaine Dye, Atl - 2 - 6
7. Alan Benes, Stl - - 5 5
